descriptions.leanBeef: Frozen Australian lean beef, low in fat and suitable for hot pot, stir-fry, or pan-seared dishes.
descriptions.banana:
• Fresh bananas provide natural energy, potassium, and fiber for daily meals.
  • Convenient for breakfast, smoothies, or quick snacks.
  • Store in a cool, dry place and use when ripe for the best sweetness.

How to choose fresh bananas

  • Choose bananas with firm texture, even color, and no deep bruises.
  • A few small brown spots usually mean the banana is ripe and sweeter.
descriptions.guava:
• Fresh guava is crisp, fragrant, and rich in vitamin C.
  • Suitable for eating directly, juicing, or serving with dipping salt.
  • Provides fiber and supports a balanced daily diet.

How to choose fresh guava

  • Choose firm fruits with smooth skin and a light natural fragrance.
  • Avoid fruits with soft bruised spots or cracked skin.
descriptions.watermelon:
• Watermelon is refreshing, juicy, and naturally sweet.
  • Great for desserts, juice, or cooling down on hot days.
  • Provides water and light natural sweetness for the whole family.

How to choose watermelon

  • Choose fruit that feels heavy for its size and has a clear field spot.
  • Avoid cracked, bruised, or overly soft fruit.
descriptions.purpleGrapes:
• Purple grapes are sweet, juicy, and convenient for healthy snacking.
  • Serve chilled for better texture and flavor.
  • Suitable for desserts, fruit plates, or lunch boxes.

How to choose grapes

  • Choose bunches with firm berries attached to fresh green stems.
  • Avoid berries that are wrinkled, leaking, or moldy.
descriptions.hamburger: Fresh beef burger with vegetables and special sauce, ready to eat and convenient for quick meals.
descriptions.greenMango:
• Green mango is crisp with a light sour taste, suitable for dipping sauce or salads.
  • It is convenient for snacks and fresh fruit plates.
  • Keep refrigerated after cutting for better freshness.

How to choose green mango

  • Choose firm mangoes with smooth skin and no bruises.
  • Avoid fruits that are too soft or have dark sunken spots.
descriptions.australianApple:
• Australian apples are crisp, juicy, and naturally sweet.
  • Suitable for eating directly, desserts, or school snacks.
  • Rich in fiber and easy to store in the refrigerator.

How to choose apples

  • Choose firm apples with glossy skin and no bruises.
  • Avoid soft fruits or apples with cuts on the skin.
descriptions.freshOrange: Imported fresh oranges with thin peel, lots of juice, and natural sweetness.
descriptions.freshVegetables:
• Fresh vegetables provide vitamins, minerals, and fiber for balanced family meals.
  • They support a healthy diet and are suitable for soups, stir-fries, salads, and daily cooking.
  • Selected daily to help keep freshness, natural color, and good texture.

How to choose fresh vegetables

  • Choose vegetables with firm texture, natural color, and no deep bruises or wilted stems.
  • Avoid produce with strange chemical smells, dark soft spots, or overly glossy surfaces.
  • Use soon after purchase or store properly in the refrigerator to maintain freshness.
descriptions.milkBox: Pure boxed milk, rich in calcium and vitamin D, suitable for the whole family.
